title: Ledger arrangement container manifest
description: The serialized description + access manifest for one unit of arrangement: a collection, or a series inside a collection (#202). A container carries description and policy and no bytes and no identity; this schema structurally forbids any top-level `contributor_name`, `identity`, or `name` property, exactly as the record schema does (no-outing rule). A container's existence is itself disclosable material — a collection titled after the event its records document outs by aggregation even when every record inside it is sealed — which is why `policy` (who may know this container exists and read its description) is separate from `records_policy` (the ceiling over the records filed in it).

container_id.description: Stable identifier, one allow-listed path component. It becomes a filename, a URL segment, an EAD `id` attribute and an OAI-PMH `setSpec`, so the allow-list is the same one record ids use.

title.description: Human-readable title of the collection or series. Disclosed under this container's own `policy`, never under the policy of what it holds.

level.description: Two levels, not an unbounded tree: a collection is a root and a series sits directly under one. This bounds every root-to-node chain at two links, which is what makes the policy resolution a loop rather than a recursion.

parent_id.description: The collection this series belongs to; null for a collection. A collection that names a parent, or a series that does not, is refused by `ledger.arrangement.validate_container` and fails closed in `Arrangement.chain` (every record below it becomes invisible rather than unclamped).

scope_and_content.description: The archivist's scope-and-content note: whose material this is, how it came in, what is in it. A series with an empty note inherits the nearest VISIBLE ancestor's at disclosure time; the note of an ancestor a viewer may not see is never inherited through a container they may.

extent.description: Free-text extent as an archivist would write it ("4 boxes", "1 linear foot", "12 cassettes"). Deliberately not a count of the records ledger holds: a count derived from the archive would change as sealed material is added, which is an oracle about material the reader cannot list.

dates.description: Free-text inclusive/bulk dates as an archivist would write them ("1987-1994, bulk 1991").

policy.description: Who may know this container exists and read its own description (title, scope note, extent, dates). Narrows down the chain: a container is visible only if every container above it is.

unseal_at.description: ISO-8601 instant at which a sealed-until container's own description opens, or null.

unseal_condition.description: Free-text condition for a sealed-conditional container's own description, or null.

records_policy.description: The ceiling over every record filed in this container or below it. Applied as a logical AND with the record's own policy, so it can only ever remove visibility: a broad container never widens a narrow record.

records_unseal_at.description: ISO-8601 instant at which the ceiling over this container's records lifts, or null.

records_unseal_condition.description: Free-text condition for a sealed-conditional ceiling over this container's records, or null.
